finalJustifications: Because ELB send periodic checks (HTTP to a path such as /health or TCP at the door) and, after N consecutive failures, marks the unhealthy target and cuts traffic.
Because ELB read application logs for errors 500 and removes from rotation instances with rate above the limit.
Because ELB pin the operating system via ICMP every second, detecting locks before affecting the service.
Because ELB measures the average response time of each registered target and automatically removes the slower distribution.

finalJustifications: Because Cross-Zone Load Balancing distributes requests between TODAS the instances of TODAS the AZs, regardless of where the traffic entered.
Because Cross-Zone moves the overloaded AZ instances to empty AZ, rebalancing the group's physical capacity.

Because Cross-Zone requires the same number of instances in each AZ, which forces the uniform redistribution of traffic.

Because ALB it is the new generation that replaces the NLB in all cases — AWS maintain the NLB only for legacy customers of the Classic era.

Because the only real difference is the price per hour: the two route the same protocols, and the choice is a cost decision of the project.

finalJustifications: Because one Region is a set of geographically close AZs, and each AZ has independent power, network and cooling datacenters — failure in one does not knock down the other.
Because each AZ is on a different continent, and the Region is the logical grouping that resists global energy and network disasters.
Because the AZs share the same building separated by floors, with independent generators ensuring the isolation of faults.
Because a region corresponds to a physical data center and the AZs are the isolated server rooms with their own energy inside it..

optionReasons.saa-ini-013:option:1: Users IAM permanent for third parties create long-term credentials to manage and revoke — just what you want to avoid.
optionReasons.saa-ini-013:option:2: Making public resources exposes the entire company — never the answer for consulting access.
optionReasons.saa-ini-013:option:3: Sharing administrator keys is the worst possible practice — full access and no traceability.

finalJustifications: Because a cross-account roll allows identities of the consulting account to assume temporary and delimited permissions in the company's account — without permanent credentials.
Because the role automatically creates mirrored users in the consulting account, synchronized while the access contract lasts.
Because the role grants temporary root access to consultants, automatically revoked at the end of each work session in the account.
Because the role synchronizes the passwords between the two accounts, allowing the direct login of the consultants in the console of the contracting company.
